content.title: Answers built on the models and metrics you trust
content.body: General-purpose chatbots guess at table meanings and invent joins. The analyst reads your project’s descriptions, tests, owners and certified metrics first, then writes queries against the same definitions your dashboards use, so its numbers match the ones leaders already see.

items.title: Uses certified metrics before raw tables

Explains its reasoning and the SQL it ran

image.alt: The metric loop: define, review, publish, query, cache, audit

content.title: Built for the questions people actually ask
content.body: Ask follow-ups, compare periods, break results down by any dimension and save useful answers for later. The analyst keeps track of the conversation, so each new question builds on the last one without starting over from scratch.

tabs.body: Type a question the way you would ask a colleague and get a chart, a table and a short written summary in return, usually within a few seconds.

content.title: Self-serve answers without losing control of the numbers
content.body: Data teams stay in charge of definitions and access, while everyone else gets fast, consistent answers. Fewer one-off requests reach the queue, and the ones that do are better questions.

content.title: Stay in control of definitions and access
content.body: Decide which models and metrics the analyst may use, review the questions people ask, and improve descriptions where answers fall short. Every query respects the permissions of the person asking.

quotes.quote: Our product managers ask the analyst before they file a ticket, and most of the time the answer they get matches the dashboard exactly. When it does not, the lineage shows us which description to improve, so the next answer is better for everyone who asks a similar question.

We could not allow a tool that guessed at regulated figures. Because the analyst only uses certified metrics and shows its SQL, our risk team approved it after one review, and finance now uses it daily for variance questions that used to take an afternoon.

content.title: Teams getting faster answers from the data they already trust
content.body: Early customers are cutting their request queues and giving more people direct access to reliable numbers every day.

cards.quote: The analyst answers the routine questions, which leaves our team free for the hard ones. Sales leaders used to wait two days for a pipeline breakdown; now they ask, check the lineage and move on. Our request queue shrank by half in the first month, and the questions that still reach us are the interesting ones that need a person to think them through.

cards.line: more people asking questions of trusted data each week, with no growth in the request queue

cards.quote: Answers match our dashboards because they use the same metrics. That consistency is what won our leadership team over.
Clinical managers get capacity answers in seconds, and every one of them is traceable to the source.

content.title: Ask questions from the tools your teams open every single morning
content.body: Use the analyst in chat, in your browser, in spreadsheets or inside your BI tool. Answers carry the same certified definitions wherever the question is asked.

content.body: Request access to Lattice Analyst and see how it performs on your own certified models. We will help you choose a pilot group, set the scope and review the first week of questions together.
